'''Rowland Leonard Brooks''' (February 6, 1916 – June 18, 1993)<ref name="bsst">[http://www.squaring.net/history_theory/brooks_smith_stone_tutte.html Brooks, Smith, Stone, Tutte], squaring.net, retrieved 2010-07-30.
</ref> was an English mathematician, known for proving [[Brooks's theorem]] on the relation between the [[chromatic number]] and the [[degree (graph theory)|degree]] of [[undirected graph|graphs]]. He was born in [[Lincolnshire]], [[England]], studied at [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]], [[Cambridge University]], and also worked with fellow Trinity students [[W. T. Tutte]], [[Cedric Smith (statistician)|Cedric Smith]], and [[Arthur Harold Stone]] on the problem of "[[Squaring the square]]" (partitioning [[rectangle]]s and [[Square (geometry)|square]]s into unequal squares), both under their own names and under the [[pseudonym]] [[Blanche Descartes]].<ref>{{citation|first=Alexander|last=Soifer|year=2008|title=The Mathematical Coloring Book|title-link= The Mathematical Coloring Book |publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=978-0-387-74640-1|pages=82–83}}.</ref>

After leaving Cambridge, he worked as a full-time tax inspector.<ref name="bsst"/>
